full_text:
झारखंड में सीजनल फ्लू को लेकर अलर्ट, स्वास्थ्य विभाग ने जारी की एडवाइजरी; अस्पतालों में बनेंगे आइसोलेशन वार्ड
झारखंड सरकार ने इन्फ्लूएंजा A H1N1 और H3N2 के बढ़ते मामलों को देखते हुए राज्यभर में अलर्ट जारी किया है। ...और पढ़ें
HighLights
इन्फ्लूएंजा A H1N1 और H3N2 को लेकर अलर्ट जारी।
अस्पतालों में 10 बेड के आइसोलेशन वार्ड बनाने के निर्देश।
राज्य ब्यूरो, रांची। देश के कई राज्यों दिल्ली, कर्नाटक, केरल, महाराष्ट्र और राजस्थान में इन्फ्लूएंजा A H1N1 और H3N2 के बढ़ते मामलों को देखते हुए झारखंड का स्वास्थ्य विभाग सतर्क हो गया है। हालांकि, स्वास्थ्य विभाग के अनुसार, फिलहाल झारखंड में इन्फ्लूएंजा संक्रमण की पुष्टि नहीं हुई है। एहतियात और जागरूकता के जरिए संक्रमण से बचाव संभव है।
केंद्र सरकार के स्वास्थ्य एवं परिवार कल्याण मंत्रालय से मिले निर्देशों के बाद राष्ट्रीय स्वास्थ्य मिशन, झारखंड के अभियान निदेशक शशि प्रकाश झा ने राज्य के सभी सिविल सर्जन, मेडिकल कॉलेजों और जिला सर्विलेंस पदाधिकारियों को अलर्ट रहने और लगातार निगरानी रखने का निर्देश दिया है।
एकीकृत रोग निगरानी कार्यक्रम (IDSP) के तहत राज्य सर्विलेंस पदाधिकारी डॉ. प्रदीप कुमार सिंह की देखरेख में पूरे राज्य में ILI (सर्दी, खांसी और बुखार) और SARI (गंभीर श्वसन संक्रमण) के मामलों की रोजाना निगरानी की जा रही है। इन मामलों की रिपोर्टिंग IHIP पोर्टल पर भी सुनिश्चित की जा रही है।
रिम्स और एमजीएम में जांच की सुविधा
संक्रमण से निपटने के लिए राज्य स्तर पर तैयारियां शुरू कर दी गई हैं। इन्फ्लूएंजा A H1N1 और H3N2 की जांच की सुविधा रिम्स, रांची और एमजीएम, जमशेदपुर में उपलब्ध कराई गई है।
इसके साथ ही सभी जिला अस्पतालों और मेडिकल कॉलेजों में संभावित और संक्रमित मरीजों के इलाज के लिए कम से कम 10 बेड का आइसोलेशन वार्ड चिन्हित करने का निर्देश दिया गया है।
अस्पतालों में PPE किट, N95 मास्क, ट्रिपल लेयर मास्क, VTM किट, जरूरी दवाएं, ऑक्सीजन उपकरण और वेंटिलेटर की पर्याप्त व्यवस्था रखने को कहा गया है।
अस्पतालों की OPD में आने वाले ILI और SARI मरीजों की अनिवार्य स्क्रीनिंग की जाएगी। इसके लिए डॉक्टरों और स्वास्थ्यकर्मियों को मास्क पहनने के भी सख्त निर्देश दिए गए हैं।
लोगों को जागरूक कर रहा स्वास्थ्य विभाग
इन्फ्लूएंजा से बचाव, इसके लक्षण और क्या करें और क्या न करें से जुड़ी जानकारी लोगों तक पहुंचाई जा रही है। आईईसी के स्टेट नोडल ऑफिसर डॉ. राहुल किशोर सिंह ने बताया कि जागरूकता सामग्री के जरिए लोगों को संक्रमण से बचाव के बारे में जानकारी दी जा रही है।
इन लोगों को विशेष सावधानी बरतने की सलाह
स्वास्थ्य विभाग की एडवाइजरी के अनुसार, बुजुर्ग, 5 वर्ष तक के छोटे बच्चे, गर्भवती महिलाएं और पुरानी गंभीर बीमारियों से ग्रसित लोग संक्रमण के प्रति अधिक संवेदनशील हैं। इसलिए इनका विशेष ध्यान रखने की जरूरत है।
राज्य सर्विलेंस पदाधिकारी डॉ. प्रदीप कुमार सिंह ने बताया कि सभी सरकारी और निजी अस्पतालों को मरीजों का डेटा IHIP पोर्टल पर नियमित रूप से दर्ज करने का निर्देश दिया गया है।
संक्रमण से बचने के लिए क्या करें?
स्वास्थ्य विभाग ने लोगों को संक्रमण से बचाव के लिए कुछ सावधानियां बरतने की सलाह दी है:
- भीड़-भाड़ वाली जगहों पर जाते समय मास्क पहनें।
- छींकते या खांसते समय रुमाल या कपड़े से मुंह और नाक ढंकें।
- शरीर में पानी की मात्रा बनाए रखने के लिए पर्याप्त तरल पदार्थ पिएं।
लक्षण दिखने पर लोगों से तुरंत अपने नजदीकी सदर अस्पताल या सरकारी चिकित्सा संस्थान से संपर्क करने की अपील की गई है।
स्वास्थ्य संबंधी किसी भी परामर्श, लक्षण दिखने पर सलाह या सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सुविधाओं की जानकारी के लिए राज्य सरकार के 24 घंटे उपलब्ध हेल्पलाइन नंबर 104 पर संपर्क किया जा सकता है।

Manitoba government rolls out millions in tariff relief measures
The Manitoba government has announced millions of dollars in new relief measures to support businesses and workers as they deal with the effects of an ongoing tariff war between Canada and the U.S.
Supports include $50M for trade resilience loan program, cabinet minister says

The Manitoba government has announced millions of dollars in new relief measures to support businesses and workers as they deal with the effects of an ongoing tariff war between Canada and the U.S.
The support includes additional money to increase existing programs and funds for new initiatives aimed at things such as interprovincial trade missions for Manitoba alcohol producers and providing wage subsidy support for employers.
The new measures also allow businesses to defer provincially administered tax payments from Sept. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026.
"These initiatives altogether are a comprehensive suite of programs to ensure that our economy in Manitoba will weather the storm of Donald Trump's tariffs and become stronger throughout it," Jamie Moses — the minister of business, mining, trade and jobs creation — said at a news conference at the Manitoba Legislative Building on Friday.
"We continue to support labour leaders, continue to support provincial trade barriers being broken down and opening up more markets domestically here in Canada."
The tariff relief measures include $50 million for the Manitoba trade resilience loan program to provide repayable working capital financing at low interest rates. They also include $13.7 million to establish a tariff workforce stabilization and youth employment program to provide wage subsidy supports to employers, and $500,000 to support interprovincial trade missions for alcohol producers and craft breweries, the province said in a news release.
The measures also include a $500,000 increase in the export support program, $500,000 to Canadian Manufacturers and Exporters to expand its made-in-Manitoba initiative, and $250,000 to enhance existing export advisory services to support export readiness and market development, the release said.
The province said some support will come through the Manitoba Agricultural Service Corporation, which will increase its operating credit guarantee program to $3 million for individuals, corporations and partnerships, and increase the guaranteed portion of loans under that program and the diversification loan guarantee program to 33.33 per cent.
The corporation will also expand eligibility for its diversification loan guarantee program to include grain and oilseed operations and allow "investment in primary agricultural infrastructure in Manitoba" as an eligible purpose, increase the loan amount under that program to $5 million (up from $1.5 million), and work with honey producers to develop and implement targeted supports for that sector, the release said.
The province said the latest escalation in the Canada-U.S. trade war, after talks collapsed, is expected to affect Manitoba industries such as agri-food, transportation, construction, wholesale trade, aerospace, forestry, machinery and beverages.
Moses said the total operational cost of the programming the province is putting forward will be over $100 million. He was flanked by more than a dozen people — including representatives from business, labour and agriculture, and NDP caucus colleagues.
Plan lauded by business, labour, agriculture
Bram Strain, president and CEO of the Business Council of Manitoba, was at the news conference. He said the kinds of programs the government announced will provide the certainty businesses need right now.
"The speed [at] which you are moving, filling gaps that were left by federal programming, that's what this is about," Strain said.
Kevin Rebeck, president of the Manitoba Federation of Labour, said many families of people working in industries such as steel, manufacturing and food production have been worried about what effect tariffs will have. He was glad to see the province recognize the importance of acknowledging those workers alongside businesses.
"For our economy to remain strong and for businesses to succeed, we need to make sure that working people have money in their pockets to spend in our local economy," Rebeck said.
Jill Verwey, president of Keystone Agricultural Producers, said her organization was also pleased to see the province's commitment to working with sectors hit hard by tariffs, including honey and beekeepers.
"The U.S. is Manitoba's top trading partner, and we value this longstanding, mutually beneficial trading relationship. However, actions that disrupt the free flow of goods carry real cost to both sides of the border, in any tariff level," she said.
The province said in its news release beekeepers will be eligible for all the agriculture business supports announced Friday, including loan guarantees for operations and expansions.
Opposition unimpressed
Opposition Leader Obby Khan said he wasn't impressed by the plan Moses unveiled, saying loans businesses have to pay back and a tax deferral that only gives them a few months of breathing room won't help them in the long term.
"We see this repeat pattern over and over again with this government and this minister, right? It's a big flashy announcement, there's no details, and there's no long-term support for these businesses," Khan told CBC's Up to Speed host Faith Fundal on Friday afternoon.
He said businesses need more long-term, reliable relief, and called on the government to do more to remove interprovincial trade barriers.

[Sportschosun Jo Min-jung reporter] Jae-gyun Hwang, who has ended his professional baseball career, will hold an early retirement celebration with his family on the day his official retirement ceremony was postponed because of the heat wave.
In episode 413 of the Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation (MBC) variety show "Omniscient Interfering View," which airs on the 29th, a cheerful yet touching day with Hwang and his family unfolds after they hear the sudden news that the retirement ceremony has been postponed.
The ceremony had originally been scheduled for that day. But the event was put on hold because of the heat wave, disrupting not only Hwang's plans but also those of his family. Since they had already ordered food and a cake for the ceremony, they decided to gather as planned and hold an "early retirement celebration party" instead.
Hwang's parents, his younger sister and her husband, and his nephew all came together as the "Hwang family." The table was filled with steamed king crab, beef, and even his father's curry and rolled omelet, which Hwang loved as a child. As his longtime No. 1 fans, the family was more disappointed than anyone that the official ceremony had been delayed. They even joked, "Since the retirement ceremony was canceled, cancel the retirement announcement too," revealing their honest wish for him to return to active play and drawing laughter.
The family also looked back on Hwang's 30-year baseball career. In particular, the show will reveal the story of how Hwang, who had ranked first in his class throughout his school years, chose baseball over academics.
Hwang inherited athletic DNA from his parents, both former national tennis players, and showed exceptional talent from an early age. His father, who recognized his son's potential, reportedly visited a baseball coach in person and opened the door for him to pursue a career as a player.
His mother, however, initially opposed her son becoming a baseball player. The broadcast will also reveal the real reason the former national team athlete mother objected to his athletic career, as well as the choice the family made at the time. Hwang's baseball journey, which began with the support of his family, continued for about 30 years. Stories shared directly by the family, who watched his growth and career up close, are expected to add meaning to the retirement party.
Hwang's special affection for his nephew will also be revealed. He hopes the child will grow up to become the "Shohei Ohtani of Korea," and has continued to support him generously. Hwang has reportedly bought about 1 million won worth of clothes for his nephew at once, and even handed his personal card to his younger sister. His image as a big-hearted uncle who never hesitates to spend for his nephew is expected to surprise the panelists.
Although the official retirement ceremony has been postponed because of the unexpected heat wave, the family will celebrate Hwang's new beginning early by sharing carefully prepared food and memories.
Hwang and his family's "early retirement celebration party" will air on MBC's "Omniscient Interfering View" at 11:10 p.m. on the 29th.
